Prevention: LMV is transmitted by several aphid species that can acquire the disease through infected plants.
Protect nurseries with floating row covers to protect seedlings from aphids or produce lettuce under a sheltered environment.
Remove host plants and weeds from nurseries, plots, the edges of the field and between rows to eliminate the virus or aphid sinks and avoid aphid propagation.
The disease is also transmitted by seeds so only use certified disease-free seeds.
The association of lettuce with flowering plant strips ( Gypsophila grandiflora , Coriandrum sativum , and
Trifolium resupinatum ), attract adult syrphids whose larvae can control aphids.
Bury crop residues immediately after harvest to avoid aphid populations build-up.
Leave a fallow period of 2 weeks between crops.
Monitoring: Symptoms can vary depending on the lettuce variety, strain of the virus, age of the crop when infected and environmental conditions:
Young plants from infected seeds show a mosaic or mottling pattern and don’t develop.
Plants infected later show interveinal discoloration and leaf distortion (twisted or in head lettuce, outer older leaves curve back away from the head).
Plants can be stunted, and developing heads may be deformed and show some necrotic flecks.
Monitor twice a week for aphid presence, and specifically the edge of the field.
In seedlings, treat rapidly if the population is high.
In older plants, treat before the development of the head, where aphids hide.
LMV is a major pathogen of lettuce so apply control measures rapidly when symptoms or aphids are observed.
Direct Control: If infection occurs in nurseries, eliminate infected seedlings.
In the early morning or late evening, apply a solution of neem oil and soap (160-200 cc neem: 100g of soap in 20L of water) to leaves to slow down the spread of the virus.
